A truncated area-under-the-curve (AUC) metric was calculated by summing estimates of percentage signal change (100 × β coefficient/baseline) across an 8 s window after delivery of the regulation instruction (5–12 s, inclusive).

source_definition.value: Emotion-regulation instruction condition on negative trials, with three levels: increase, attend, and decrease.

spans.text: participants were trained to follow one of three instructions during each picture trial: “increase,” “decrease,” or “attend.”

hrf_model.value: Finite impulse response/full deconvolution basis with 16 time points

spans.text: Single-subject general linear models (GLMs) using full deconvolution (B. D. Ward, Deconvolution Analysis of fMRI Time Series Data , http://afni.nimh.nih.gov/afni ) were performed to estimate the impulse response function

model_settings.value: Single-subject GLMs modeled six conditions with stick-function predictors, included normative unpleasantness ratings and six motion parameters as covariates, applied a 0.02 Hz high-pass filter, and summarized percentage signal change using an 8-second AUC window from 5–12 seconds after instruction onset.

spans.text: In addition, to account for variability in stimulus unpleasantness across conditions, we modeled normative ratings of unpleasantness gleaned from the IAPS dataset.

software.value: AFNI version 2.40e; follow-up GLM and pairwise analyses in SPSS version 12.

description.value: Participants used cognitive reappraisal to increase, decrease, or attend to negative affect while viewing unpleasant photographs.

Participants were cued to amplify the intensity of their negative affect in response to unpleasant pictures by imagining themselves or a loved one experiencing the depicted situation or imagining a more extreme outcome.

spans.text: The instruction to increase, presented via pneumatic headphones (Avotec), served as a cue to amplify the intensity of their negative affect

description.value: Participants were instructed to maintain attention to the unpleasant picture without changing their negative affective experience; this served as the attention control condition.

spans.text: on attend trials, participants were instructed to maintain their attention to the picture without changing their negative affective experience

description.value: Participants were cued to reduce the intensity of their negative affect in response to unpleasant pictures by viewing the situation as fake or unreal or imagining that it had a different, less negative outcome.

spans.text: the instruction to decrease signified the cue to reduce the intensity of their negative affect

Stimulus presentation was accomplished using the E-Prime software suite (Psychology Software Tools, Pittsburgh, PA) while visual stimulation was delivered via a fiber-optic goggle system (Avotec, Stuart, FL) interfaced with an eye-tracking system (SensoMotoric Instruments, Needham, MA) to measure pupil dilation during the scan session.

stimuli.value: Digital color photographs from the International Affective Picture System

instructions.value: On each picture trial, participants followed one of three instructions: increase negative affect by imagining themselves or a loved one experiencing the depicted situation or imagining a more extreme outcome; decrease negative affect by viewing the situation as fake or unreal or imagining a different, less negative outcome; or attend by maintaining attention to the picture without changing their negative affective experience.
